column1: # Shared vectors for the pieces of an instant-cache file name and the
# cache-read status code, beyond the path key (cache_key_vectors.tsv). The
# shells must name a cache file exactly as the agent writes it
# Format: tab-separated, the first column names the row kind:
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored; extra columns MUST be
# ignored. The whole-column token \e means the EMPTY string, and an input
# column uses the mini escape scheme of json_escape_vectors.tsv (backslash
# first: \\ -> one backslash, \n -> LF, \r -> CR, \t -> tab). `expected` is
# literal. Every reader MUST fail on an unknown kind, or if this file is
# Status codes are __gpy_read_instant_cache's contract: 0 fresh hit, 1 miss,
# 2 stale hit, 4 fresh variant-fallback hit, 6 stale variant-fallback hit.
# Other codes are never produced (Bash/Zsh test bits, Fish compares values).
# Known divergence, deliberately absent: a non-ASCII prev_bg under a non-UTF-8
# locale. Rust and Fish map per character (`xé1ß` -> `x_1_`); Bash and Zsh
# map per byte under LC_ALL=C (`x__1__`). Theme colours are ASCII names and
# hex, so no real prev_bg reaches it.
# rows against `prev_bg_token` and `position_suffix`, so an edited expected
# value fails there too. Rust checks every `token` row, and a `suffix` row
# whose two flag cells are `true`, `false` or `\e` (`\e` is false). It skips
# `suffix` rows with other spellings (`TRUE`, `1`), which test the shells'
